evaluation: Forward-chaining (time-ordered) validation on the cleaned 15-min series: 5 blocks between 2021-10-26 and 2021-12-09, each predicted by a model (profile and ridge) fitted only on data ending at least 1 h before the block; pooled RMSE 0.79 kWh per 15-min interval over 1,641 intervals (blocks 0.47-1.04), versus 2.35 for 1-h persistence and 0.97 for a clock profile alone. On the same last-444-interval window that bemlops used as its test set (2021-11-12 to 2021-12-09) the model gets 0.73 vs 0.80 for the bemlops gradient-boosting model and 2.55 for persistence. I quote 0.85 rather than 0.79 because only about 27 usable weekdays exist, one public-holiday schedule (2021-11-04, RMSE 2.45 that day) is inside the blocks, and later months may behave differently.
data_findings: Shape: 10,800 rows at 5-min steps, 35 columns, 2021-09-07..2021-12-09 (a +08:00 offset in the timestamp text, stripped and treated as local wall-clock time). Predictions are returned on 15-min interval starts (energy = sum of the three 5-min values).

Time axis problems: rows are not in order (a 30-row block 2021-10-28 21:00-23:25 is stored reversed) and 288 rows (2021-11-15 01:10 .. 11-16 01:05) are exact duplicates; sorted and de-duplicated in code. Large gaps: every weekend is absent, 2021-09-09, 2021-09-23 14:00 .. 09-24 01:55, 2021-10-02..10-24 (23 days) and 2021-11-18..12-08 (21 days). Only ~36 distinct days exist, ~27 with a trustworthy target.

Operation: the AHU/cooling coil runs on a fixed weekday schedule (about 08:05-18:35); with the valve open the chilled-water energy is ~2.3 kWh per 5 min (1.2 minimum), otherwise exactly 0. The only schedule deviation is 2021-11-04 (Deepavali holiday): AHU started 10:05 and stopped 17:40. The clock profile therefore explains most of the variance; the last quarter-hour block before shutdown (18:15 interval) is spiky and is the largest source of error.

Target faults (all set to missing, never to zero and never filled): 17 placeholder values of -999; chilled_water_energy reads exactly 0 for five weeks (2021-09-21 .. 2021-10-26 10:25, ~1,290 five-minute rows) although the coil valve command is 15-65% and the fan runs normally = meter outage; the same dropout on 2021-11-17 15:15-18:35 (erratic values from 14:15 and a 13.6 kWh catch-up reading); a meter value stuck at 0.484552 from 2021-11-03 18:40 to 2021-11-04 10:10 while the AHU was off. Rule used (causal, row-wise): reading < 0.5 kWh while valve command > 15% = fault; a non-zero reading identical to the previous sample = stuck. With the valve open the real 5-min value is never below ~1.2 kWh, so the rule does not remove real data.

air_temperature (room) switches from degC (~28) to degF (~81) from 2021-11-08 onwards (26% of rows); values > 45 are converted to degC (same guard for off-coil and outdoor temperature in case other points switch later). outdoor_relative_humidity contains the text OFFLINE (14 rows) and sits at 99.9 for hours in rain (kept, treated as possible saturation); dry_bulb_temp has single-sample spikes up to 50.7 degC (limited by clipping standardised features).

Unreliable or unused points: wifi_connected_devices is stuck at 2 for 17.5 h on the last day, occupant_count/occupant_presence are 0 for whole days (11-04, 11-05, 11-17), supply_air_flow and damper_position are NaN for weeks or change regime (1,943 -> ~900 CMH on 09-13, 0 on 10-25), offcoil_temp_setpoint is constant. None of these were used. voc, noise, light, PM2.5, CO2 etc. were not needed.

The level drifts between days (mean energy of on-intervals 4.8 kWh per 15 min in the first week of September vs 6-8 later), so the model corrects the clock profile with the recent deviation (last 2 h, last day, last 3 days) rather than relying on the profile alone.

Weekends/holidays never appear in training. Assumption built into predict(): on Saturdays/Sundays the forecast is persistence of the last usable value that is at least 1 h old (an idle AHU is forecast as idle, a running AHU is followed with a 1 h lag). Public holidays on weekdays are not modelled.
usability: Non-causal cleaning in the default prepare(): mask_stuck flags a whole stretch once it is >= stuck_hours long (so earlier samples of the stretch change status when later data arrive) and mask_spikes works on single-sample spikes, which by its description needs the next sample. ForecastModel.predict re-runs the same prepare() on live data, so a forecast can change when later data arrive, which contradicts the only-past-data guarantee and would fail a truncation test. I had to call prepare(mask_stuck=False, mask_spikes=False) and write my own causal masks. The skill/docs should say which prepare steps look ahead.

check_data false negatives: it caught -999, the text OFFLINE, 288 duplicate timestamps, unsorted rows, spikes and even the single stuck target stretch (0.484552 for 15 h 20 min), but it did NOT notice that the target meter read 0 for five weeks while the coil valve (a declared input) was open and the fan ran. A check such as target is 0 while its driver is on (or a very long all-zero stretch in an energy column) would have found the biggest problem in this file; the stuck check apparently ignores zeros.

check_data false positives on legitimately held values: off-coil air temperature is frozen at 26.1402 for 6.5 h whenever the fan is off, and outdoor RH sits at 99.9 for 17 h in rain; both are reported as stuck and prepare() would blank them. mask_stuck is global, there is no per-column switch (only accept() or turning masking off for all columns).

Mixed units inside one column are reported misleadingly: air_temperature changes from degC to degF part-way (24-26% of rows > 45), and the error says out_of_range ... too many to be sensor glitches: check the declaration, although the declaration (degC) is right for 74% of the data. The unit_mismatch hint (which unit fits) is not given because the column is mixed. A message such as values > 45 fit degF from 2021-11-08 and a helper that converts only the offending rows would help.
Timestamps with a UTC-offset suffix (2021-09-07 00:00 +08:00) are not covered by the skill's timestamp advice; I stripped the offset myself before passing timestamp_format.

Energy resampling: prepare() aggregates energy with a sum; from the line r.sum(min_count=1) I saw in prepare.py (while grepping for sum/energy) this returns a partial sum when 1-2 of the three 5-min readings in an interval are missing, silently understating the energy. I pre-aggregated to 15 min myself with a strict/scaled rule. Suggest requiring a full interval or logging a warning.

The feature set is fixed and not documented in help(): target lags t-4..t-7, t-96, t-672 (one week), a 1-day rolling mean of the target, and declared inputs at t-4. There is no argument to choose lags, add calendar features (minute-of-day, day-of-week, holiday) or a clock-profile baseline; I had to create minute_of_day myself and declare it known_ahead. The one-week lag is useless for a series with no weekends and 3-week gaps. For a scheduled on/off load the best model was a time-of-day profile + ridge on the recent deviation, which I had to build outside bemlops (0.73 vs 0.80 RMSE for the bemlops gbm on the same window; the bemlops ridge scored 1.25 on validation).

Baselines are weak for scheduled loads: persistence (RMSE 2.1-2.5 kWh) and same-time-yesterday (1.96) make the gbm look strong (skill 0.69), but a plain time-of-day mean profile already gives 0.97. A time-of-day-mean baseline in the defaults would make the skill number honest.

fit() is slow and silent: ridge+gbm with n_iter 4-6 on 3,000 rows took 438-566 s (the machine was heavily loaded by other jobs, so absolute times are inflated) and the default 3-model search did not finish within 10 minutes, with no progress output; a verbose/time-budget option would help. PrepareOptions (fill_limit, stuck_hours, ...) is only discoverable by inspecting the dataclass: help(Project.prepare) just says Options: mask_stuck, mask_spikes, fill_limit, ...

Not used in the deliverable: Registry/promotion and ForecastModel.predict (I did save a run with save_run(); its model card is in bemlops_run/). I did not rely on ForecastModel.predict() in model.py because of the look-ahead preparation above, the validation step that can raise InvalidInputData on a new fault at scoring time, and the sklearn import time; model.py re-implements the cleaning and feature building with numpy/pandas only and loads a small JSON artifact.
model_summary: model.py: causal cleaning -> 15-min grid (energy = sum of three 5-min values) -> forecast for interval T = weekday time-of-day mean profile at T + ridge correction on the deviation from that profile over intervals <= T-60 min (lags 1-2 h, last 2 h / 1 day / 3 day mean deviation) and on 1-h-old outdoor temperature, RH, solar, off-coil temperature, valve command and room temperature. Profile and coefficients are in model_artifacts.json (fit on all of train.csv by train_final.py). The returned index is tz-naive local interval start; it covers every 15-min interval present in the file plus the next 4 intervals after the last one. predict() runs in about 1-4 s.
causality_check: work/test_causal.py: for 25 target intervals (start-up, shut-down, days after gaps, duplicate and reversed-row periods) the forecast from the full file equals the forecast from a file truncated at T-45 min and from a file in which every value at/after T-45 min was replaced by garbage (24 of 24 interval-aligned cases identical to 1e-9; the 25th case was a non-aligned timestamp in my test list).
